title: Dev/Prod Parity: One Frontend, Two Backends That Behave the Same — Check

questions.prompt: What makes local development behave like production in Agronomy Studio?
questions.explanation: Both the local mock and the production function wrap the same domain modules, so observable behavior matches and drift is avoided.
options: The mock server reimplements each endpoint's behavior by hand
The local mock and the production function both call the same `netlify/lib` modules
Production and local both run on Netlify's cloud
The frontend detects the environment and switches logic

questions.prompt: Environment parity is fundamentally about identical source files in both environments.
questions.explanation: False — parity is about identical observable behavior (the same contract). The transport shell differs; the shared module guarantees the behavior matches.

questions.prompt: What is the maintenance discipline required for the dev/prod routing to stay in sync?
questions.explanation: Routing must be updated in both places; keeping the table small (one gateway entry) makes this dual-view discipline sustainable.
options: Treat the `netlify.toml` redirects and the mock's path matching as two views of one routing table
Run all tests only in production
Hard-code service URLs into the frontend
